children.translated_text: Mercury is the metal that consists of all things, by which <s>Umāpati</s> is pleased.

children.text: kiṃ punar bahunoktena tv anyathā tena tasya kim ||
children.translated_text: Why say much more? Otherwise, what use is that to him?
Grinding is to be done in a moon-shaped vessel, with the liṅga placed within.
When joined with the divine herb, its heating in a puṭa is productive of ease.
At the time when mercury is successfully prepared, rasa, having the form of metal, is auspicious.
The one by whom it is purified becomes satisfied and is unconquerable even by the thirty gods.
In a pleasant place, in good health, on an excellent and auspicious day,

children.text: tatra kāryam idaṃ spaṣṭam ekānte suvicāritam ||
children.translated_text: this work should be done there clearly, in solitude, after careful consideration.
One should take and finely grind haritāla equal to half a tulā in weight.
When dry, mixed with the juices of bhṛṅga in equal measure, it should be subjected to a puṭa.
Afterward it should be ground finely and kept motionless for three days.
Dried without sun, apāmārga should receive three puṭas.

children.text: sūkṣmaṃ niṣpīḍayet paścāc chāyāśuṣkaṃ tu sarvadā
children.translated_text: Then it should be finely pressed out, always dried in the shade.
Payovallī should be treated with nine puṭas and, when very dry, ground down.

children.text: atha puṣpīṃ samāgṛhya śvetāṃ ca girikarṇikām
children.translated_text: Then, taking puṣpī and the white girikarṇikā,
one should make a śataṭaṅkī juice and mix it with what has been shade-dried.
Śambhu, arkavallī, vellakāra, and suśīrakī also,
mixed with nāgavallī juices, separately with śataṭaṅkī juices,
after making an eleventh puṭa, should be applied with tālaka.

children.text: dvayor vimiśritaṃ sūkṣmaṃ lepaṃ tālena pīḍayet ||
children.translated_text: The two, finely mixed together, should be pressed as a paste with tāla.

children.text: etayor yogaṃ saṃgṛhya rasenaikena vā punaḥ
children.translated_text: Taking the combination of these two, or again with a single portion of mercury,
while it is being carried through six puṭas, it must be carefully covered.

children.text: puṣṭāṃ kumārīṃ bahulārasaṃ ca niṣpīḍya teṣāṃ rasamūlakena
children.translated_text: Having pressed the juices of full-grown kumārī and bahulā, with the root-juice of those plants,

children.text: gopanīyaṃ rasadhātumuttamaṃ bho narendra kuru hemavartanam ||
children.translated_text: one should preserve the excellent mercury-metal. O king, perform the turning into gold.
When hiṅgula has been firmly compressed and then combined with kumārī eleven times,

children.text: sūkṣmavastragalitā sutālake miśrake bhavati niścalo rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: filtered through a fine cloth and mixed with purified tālaka, the mercury becomes fixed.
Pattrahaṃsagamanī, gajadhvajī, lajjakā, arkanamitā, and anāmikā,

children.text: arkaviśvam iti pakṣayute vai vallake daśadaśāṣṭasaṃyute ||
children.translated_text: together with arka and viśva, in the fortnightly mixture, in vallaka with measures ten, ten, and eight,

children.text: śuṣka ātapaṃ vinā nipīḍitaḥ vardhito janakajātravīrase
children.translated_text: dried without sun and pressed, increased with the heroic juice of janakajātra,
one should make a very firm rasāyana and place it on arka, pippalī, and jaṭādhara.

children.text: tāḍayettu payasi guṇātmake kārayettu guṭikāṃ śubhālaye
children.translated_text: One should strike it in milk endowed with good qualities and make a pill in an auspicious place.

children.text: saptavāritaritaṃ śubhamastu vo dhātubhedavad iha niścalam ||
children.translated_text: May what has crossed seven times be auspicious for you; here it is fixed like a metal-piercing agent.

children.text: kāritāṃ ca subhagāṃ sukūpikāṃ nirvraṇāṃ ca sudṛḍhāṃ samṛdhayet
children.translated_text: A fine little flask should be made, flawless and very strong, and properly prepared.

children.text: tasyā madhye niveśayedidaṃ mudrayantu sudṛḍhaṃ kūpikāmukham ||
children.translated_text: This should be placed inside it, and the mouth of the flask should be sealed very firmly.
It should be kept above the fire for twenty-seven yāmas.
One should inspect it with a mind fixed on <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Bhavā</s>, intent on the single skill of mixed medicines.
It should be struck that long, until it binds into a small lump.
The red pill, staying inside the flask, gives the potency of mercury.

children.text: yadā ca paśyed aruṇānibhāṃ śubhāṃ prabhātabālāruṇatārkakāntim
children.translated_text: When one sees it auspicious, reddish, with the splendor of the young rising sun at dawn,
shining at the top of the firm flask, then this pill is to be obtained quickly by the fortunate.

children.text: guṭikā ca rasāyanī śubhā sulabhā mānasasaṃyutatatparaiḥ
children.translated_text: The auspicious rasāyana pill is easily obtained by those who are intent and mentally composed,
by those purified by merit made in a former birth; the gold-destroying pill is an ocean of milk.
O goddess, sulfur should then be impregnated in the juice of niśācara.

children.text: tamatra saptavāraṃ tu dvipadyāśca rasena tu ||
children.translated_text: Here one should do that seven times, and with the juice of dvipadī as well.
By a coating on a sheet of silver, half and half becomes like gold.
When the sulfur in this is evenly digested, the mercury becomes capable of piercing a hundredfold.

children.text: tadrase gandhakaṃ dattvā patralepe ravau hate
children.translated_text: Having put sulfur into that juice, when the sun-metal is destroyed by coating the sheet,
then one should carry it threefold within the silver.
When half gold is mixed in, the gold matrix comes to equality.
Tālaka should be impregnated seven times with the juices of niśācara.
With that alone one should kill tin, and then carry it off with silver as the supreme process.

children.text: taṃ tāraṃ bhāvayetsūtaṃ tatsūtaṃ bandhanaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: One should impregnate that silver with mercury; that mercury becomes a binding agent.
By that alone, merely as a coating, it becomes sixty-fourfold.

children.text: śulvaṃ tu dāpayettārais tattāraṃ kāñcanaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Copper should be made to receive silver; that silver becomes gold.
In that silver there arises the excellent thing, granting the accomplishment of dharma, desire, and wealth.
The oil from the fruit of niśācara should be taken in a pātāla apparatus.
With that oil, O queen of gods, the wise man should contract the mercury.
At that very moment, O goddess, there arises a great mercury preparation bound by puṭa.
With kaṭu and ṭaṅkaṇa a liṅga should be made, O fair-faced one.
With it the contraction and killing should be performed, exceedingly wonderful.
The sun-metal, placed seven times in the juice of niśācara,
becomes free of blackness through that and takes on the brilliance of gold.

children.text: tato rasasamaṃ grāhyaṃ tena siktaṃ tu vāpitam
children.translated_text: Then an equal amount of mercury should be taken; sprinkled and sown with that,
mercury pierces a tenth part, and tenfold or a hundredfold as well.
A hundred pierces a lakh; a thousand becomes capable of piercing a crore.
One should grind a tenth part with it and make the body depart.
With a tenth part, by the equal substance described before, it becomes capable of piercing a lakh.
In that juice, having directly melted sulfur, one should again dissolve it.
By that alone, merely as a coating, O beloved, the eighteen kinds of skin disease,
hemorrhoids, fistula, lūtā, and diseases of the head are destroyed.
The leaves of niśācara should be made into a fine powder.
Ten palas of the powder should also be impregnated with bhūdhātrī.
Having stirred it with ghee and honey, one should place it in a new vessel.
It should be deposited in a heap of grain for three weeks, O mistress of the gods.
By the mere eating of it, one becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair.
With use for half a month, this becomes directly manifest, my dear.
By his urine and feces, copper becomes gold.
With use for only a month, lead becomes gold.
For this powder of bark, the limit of the characteristics is as stated before.
Again I shall teach another very rare binding of mercury.
She who is the mother of the three worlds is the chief among herbs.
By mere contact with her, mercury remains fixed.
When it has been rubbed for a week with the juice of that great herb,
and when it has been sweated, heated, and thoroughly rubbed with the juice of the great herb,
through two weeks of rubbing with her juice, O honored by heroes,
the mercury becomes visibly capable of piercing a lakh, and all metal becomes gold.
In three weeks, O goddess of gods, it pierces ten lakhs.
It grants khecarī-siddhi, whose range is unobstructed.
And in the fourth week the great mercury pierces a crore.
By the juice of the great herb itself there may be life for the dead.
With this one should kill the mercury; make it into the five states, my dear.
Then one should have it rubbed on the hands and feet of the dead person.
Even into one dead, life enters; no doubt should be entertained here.
Again I shall teach another excellent binding of mercury.
By the juice of narasāra alone, mercury is killed in an instant.
Having given the juice of narasāra together with the dust of dvipadī,
by the end of the day it comes to fixation and pierces all metals.
When lead six times its quantity has been digested by the juice of narasāra alone,
one should impregnate the stone in that juice together with the dust of dvipadī.

children.text: nirgandhā jāyate sā tu ghātayettena pannagam
children.translated_text: It becomes odorless; with that one should kill lead.

children.text: tāre tāmre tu tallepāt koṭivedhīsamena tu ||
children.translated_text: By smearing that on silver or copper, it equals one that pierces a crore.
One should separately impregnate it seven times in the juice of narasāra and in milk.
In the apparatus called Vidyādhara, rasendra comes to take the morsel.

children.text: jīryate gaganaṃ devi nirmukhaṃ carati kṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: Mica is digested, O goddess, and, mouthless, it moves at once,
by the juice of narasāra alone and by the juice of siṃhatuṇḍa.
Divine gold is produced by the sprinkling of the sun-substance.
After putting madder and red sandalwood into the juice of narasāra,
one should rub it afterwards in its own juice and sprinkle the lead, O goddess.
After seven applications, that divine gold is certainly produced.
Rasaka should be impregnated seven times with the juices of narasāra.

children.text: tadrasaṃ rasakaṃ caiva tīkṣṇalohaṃ ca pannagam ||
children.translated_text: That juice, rasaka, sharp iron, and lead,
one should rub together in one place with the juice of narasāra itself.
At that very moment the binding of mercury and rasaka takes place.

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ nāgaṃ tathā śulvaṃ rasakena tu rañjayet
children.translated_text: One should color sharp iron, lead, and copper with rasaka.
All of it becomes gold, with a luster like a kūrmāṇḍaka.
Again I shall teach another very rare binding of mercury.

children.text: sabījā cauṣadhī grāhyā kācid gulmalatā priye ||
children.translated_text: A certain bushy creeper herb, bearing seed, is to be taken, my dear.
It is the herb named Kaṅkālakhecarī, O supreme goddess.

children.text: dvitīye vāsare prāpte vajraratnaṃ tu ghātayet ||
children.translated_text: When the second day has arrived, one should kill the diamond jewel.
Whatever has been heated in fire until it has the glow of blazing flame,
one should quench the diamond jewel in the oil of Kaṅkālakhecarī.

children.text: daśavāraṃ niṣiktaṃ tu bhasmākāraṃ tu jāyate
children.translated_text: Quenched ten times, it becomes ash-like.
Make that gold-cooked seed equal to that ash.
Having added three parts borax, one should blow it in a sealed crucible.
At that very moment the fixed diamond jewel fuses into gold.
If diamond and gold, O fair-hipped one, are digested equally,
the mercury pierces a crore, O goddess, and pierces the eight metals.
Again I shall teach another very rare binding of mercury.
A certain bushy creeper herb, bearing seed, is to be taken, my dear.
The second khecarī, O goddess, is named Mantrasiṃhāsanā.
One should collect its oil in a copper vessel by means of the pātāla apparatus.

children.text: tasya tailasya madhye tu prakṣipet khecarīrasam
children.translated_text: Into the middle of that oil one should put the juice of khecarī.
One should place it within the medinī apparatus, O lovely-faced one.
By means of the former herb, O goddess, mica is brought onto the earth-ground.

children.text: rasagrāsaṃ tato dattvā marditaṃ golakaṃ kuru ||
children.translated_text: Then, having given a morsel to the mercury, one should rub it and make a pill.
With that fixed packet one should digest the mica there.

children.text: same tu gagane jīrṇe baddhaṃ tiṣṭhati sūtakam ||
children.translated_text: When an equal amount of mica has been digested, the mercury remains fixed.
When the mercury is being blown with bellows,
the form of what has been equally digested becomes like crow dung.
When double the mica has been digested, it consumes the eight metals.

children.text: jārayed gandhakaṃ sā tu tālakaṃ jārayettu sā ||
children.translated_text: It digests sulfur, and it digests orpiment.
It also digests gold and binds rasendra.
It digests all metals and precipitates all essences.

children.text: pravālaṃ jārayetsā tu gaganaṃ drāvayet tu sā
children.translated_text: It digests coral and liquefies mica.

children.text: vajraṃ ca ghātayetsā tu nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: It also kills diamond; no doubt should be entertained here.
Again I shall teach another matter by which the practitioner attains siddhi.
Having placed it in the juice of harīndarī and in a cow's horn, O lovely-faced one,
it should be deposited in a heap of grain; the mercury remains dead.
By the juice of the divine herb alone, O honored by the gods, in rasendra,

children.text: same tu kanake jīrṇe daśalakṣaṃ tu vedhayet
children.translated_text: when an equal amount of gold has been digested, it pierces ten lakhs.
With four times the amount it pierces ten crores; with six times, it pierces by mere touch.
At the seventh stage it becomes smoke-piercing; at the eighth, indeed, it is made visible.
Foolish beasts wander about, deprived of the family-herb.
From grasses, herbs, and their juices no accomplishment is produced at all.
Therefore, with every effort the family-herb must be known.
Sixty-four divine herbs are established within the family.
The deluded fools, bewildered by <s>Śiva</s>'s māyā, do not know it.
But non-divine grasses and herbs arise in mountain caves.

children.text: tṛṇauṣadhyā rasaiḥ sūto naiva baddhaḥ kadācana ||
children.translated_text: By the juices of grasses and herbs, mercury is never bound at any time.

children.text: akṣayaṃ ca varārohe vahnimadhye na tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: And, O fair-hipped one, being imperishable, it does not remain in the midst of fire.

children.text: patre pāke kaṭe chede naiva tiṣṭhati kāñcane ||
children.translated_text: In leafing, cooking, cutting, and piercing, it does not remain in gold.

children.text: na vedhaṃ pañcāśadūrdhvaṃ karoti sa rasaḥ priye
children.translated_text: That mercury, dear one, does not make penetration beyond fifty.

children.text: yāvanna baddham ekaṃ tu vikṛtaṃ tattu kāñcanam
children.translated_text: So long as it has not been bound even once, that gold is defective.
For the sake of <s>dharma</s>, wealth, desire, and liberation, one should certainly not give that, dear one.
The blessed Goddess said:

children.text: nirjīvatvaṃ gataḥ sūtaḥ kathaṃ jīvaṃ dadāti saḥ
children.translated_text: When mercury has become lifeless, how does it give life?

children.text: nirjīvasya tu nirjīvaḥ kathaṃ jīvayate rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: How does lifeless mercury enliven what is lifeless?
The blessed <s>Śiva</s> said:

children.text: divyauṣadhyā ca yaddevi rasendro mūrchito bhavet
children.translated_text: O Goddess, when the lord of mercury has been stupefied by the divine herb,
then mercury, free from blackness, lives, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
Mercury free from blackness removes another's death-time.

children.text: aṣṭānāṃ caiva lohānāṃ malaṃ naśyati tatkṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: And in that very instant the impurity of the eight metals perishes.
Who indeed would declare mercury that has entered the great stupefaction to be dead?
By the very juice of the divine herb, the one whose consciousness was lost is born again.
Again I shall declare another binding of mercury, O Lady.

children.text: kṣmāpālena hataṃ vajram anenaiva tu kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: Diamond killed by kṣmāpāla, and gold by this very means:
one should bind together diamond ash and gold ash, the two in one place.
Having digested it in the juice of niśācara, one should digest it with narajīva.
One should kill that mercury into ash, digested by the force of the herb.
When it is eaten through the mercury-yoga, one has prowess equal to <s>Śiva</s>.
When a man has eaten one tolaka, he becomes capable of transmutation by touch.
By the application of his sweat, the king of mercury is bound.
The practitioner lives for thousands of years; there is no doubt about this.
Having become equal to <s>Prajāpati</s>, he binds mercury in an instant.
By the touch of gajāri, O Goddess, kṣmāpāla too is bound.
Realgar, dear one, impregnated with the juice of koravallī,
should be digested in a sand apparatus; it becomes fixed at once.
One māṣa of a dead pellet and one māṣa of a gold pellet:
having united them and triturated them with citron acid for three days,
one should smear one karṣa of lead leaves with the mercury paste.
Divine gold is produced when the sealed crucible heating has been performed.
It should be gathered when cooled of itself, granting success in <s>dharma</s>, desire, and wealth.
O <s>Pārvatī</s>, it has milky sap, many fruits, and knots.
Named vartulaparṇī, it is praised as a binder of mercury.
The mercury placed in a sealed crucible in the juice of the ekavīrā tuber
should be blown upon with crucible fires; once bound, it is praised for eating.
From the red-kañcukī tuber one should grind it with woman's breast milk.
In the crucible, by the previous procedure, it effects the binding of mercury.
The seed of vṛścikāpattrikā, mixed with woman's breast milk,
the adept should blow upon mercury as before, for the purpose of eating.
Having brought the vajrakanda, one should place it in the mercury.

children.text: gajendrākhyaṃ puṭaṃ kṛtvā saptadhā baddhatāṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: Having made the heating called gajendra, one should bring it to boundness seven times.
One should eat that mercury in the morning; after six months one becomes immortal.
By a year-long application, one would live as long as the moon and stars.
Taking the lāṅgalī tuber and also the karkoṭī tuber,
placing the mercury within them, one should steam it and then stupefy it.
It dies, there is no doubt here, when blown upon with intense fire.
Mercury placed in a parrot-beak vessel should be heated in a closed crucible and then blown upon.
This one makes a hundredfold penetrator and indeed produces bodily perfection.
By application for six months, a man becomes diamond-bodied.
One should put mercury mixed with haṃsapadī juice inside a śukakanda.

children.text: gajendrākhyaṃ puṭaṃ dadyāt mriyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should give the heating called gajendra; it dies, there is no doubt here.
One should triturate mercury with the juice of haṃsāṅghri and śukacañcu.
Putting it inside krauñcapāda, once blown upon, one should give three heatings.
It dies, there is no doubt here; the mercury becomes capable of a hundred-thousandfold penetration.
Known as tṛṇajyotis, listen to the divine herb, dear one.
With its root, gandhābhra, and citron acid ground together,
a copper leaf smeared with it becomes gold after three heatings.
Having smeared the king of mercury with the juice of its root, O queen of the gods,
it causes mica rubbed with citron juice to be consumed in an instant.
I shall declare another herb that makes the binding of mercury, dear one.

children.text: ekameva bhavennālaṃ tasya romaṃ ca veṣṭitam ||
children.translated_text: It has a single stalk, and its hair is wrapped around it.
At its tip there is a flower resembling a parrot's beak.
And its leaves, O queen of gods, are like parrot wings.
Its tuber resembles a tortoise; its milk resembles vermilion.
Water flows from it like beeswax; having gathered that, O <s>Pārvatī</s>,
one should triturate mercury with those juices for seven days.
With that very substance one should properly transmute all metals into gold.

children.text: rasaṃ ca tālakaṃ tulyaṃ mardayed uccaṭārasaiḥ
children.translated_text: Mercury and orpiment in equal quantity should be triturated with the juices of uccaṭā.
Heated in the sun, mercury dies through the power of the divine herb.
One should pierce the seven metals with a one-lakṣa part, O fair-faced one.
A sheet of silver and copper, O goddess, becomes beautiful gold.
The lord of mercury, with the juice of <s>nalinī</s>, combined with red <s>citraka</s>,
in the quantity for smearing a sheet: silver and copper become gold.

children.text: jyotiṣmatī nāma latā yā ca kāñcanasannibhā
children.translated_text: There is a creeper named <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>, resembling gold,
rich in spreading vines, auspicious, with fruit the color of gold.
In the bright fortnight of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, having taken its excellent seed,
one should decoct it like sesame, whether by hand or even by foot.

children.text: tasya tailaṃ samādāya kumbhe tāmramaye kṣipet
children.translated_text: Taking its oil, one should place it in a copper vessel.
One should heat the vessel buried in the ground, with a chaff-fire above it.

children.text: ṣaṇmāse ca vyatikrānte tatsarvaṃ kāñcanaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: When six months have passed, all that becomes gold.
Copper becomes golden; the oil is mixed with pyrite.
I shall describe <s>dagdhārohā</s>; it brings about the binding of mercury.
It should be known as effective in contact-transmutation, accomplishing <s>dharma</s>, desire, and wealth.

children.text: śastracchinnā mahādevi dagdhā vā pāvakena tu
children.translated_text: Cut by a knife, O great goddess, or burned by fire,
that divine great herb, burned or cut, sprouts again in an instant.

children.text: śvetaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ tathā pītaṃ tasyāḥ puṣpaṃ prajāyate
children.translated_text: Its flowers arise white, black, and also yellow.
One should recognize its leaves as like those of chickpea and very well produced.
It exists on the great bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>; the <s>Gaṅgā</s> takes refuge on the mountain.

children.text: dakṣiṇe cojjayinyāṃ ca velānte'pi ca dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: It is seen also to the south, at <s>Ujjayinī</s>, and even at the seashore.
The divine juice of its bulb, together with the black stalk,

children.text: tadrasena samaṃ kṛtvā guṭikāṃ kārayed budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise man should make into a pill after combining it with an equal quantity of that juice.
With the milk of <s>snuhī</s>, one should make a coating for copper sheets.

children.text: taṃ saṃtaptaṃ niṣiñced vā vajryāṃ kanakasaprabham ||
children.translated_text: Or, when heated, he should quench it in vajrī; it becomes like gold.
Mercury, the red milk of <s>snuhī</s>, <s>kunaṭī</s>, sulphur, mica,
and realgar pierce metals with a one-thousandth part.
Taking the milk of <s>snuhī</s>, one should smelt half a niṣka of gold.
By making it into a pill, it pierces lead at that very moment.
<s>Citraka</s> is to be known as threefold: red and black are for rasāyana,
white is for pacifying disease; the best, middle, and inferior are thus distinguished.
With powder of its five parts, one should grind mercury.
One should blow it in a sealed crucible; it at once becomes an ingot.
By means of a heating-packet smeared with red <s>citraka</s> and <s>bhallāta</s> oil,
a sheet of silver and copper, O goddess, becomes beautiful gold.
With powder of red <s>citraka</s>, tin, through three and three heatings,
freed from all faults, at once comes to firmness.
The lord of mercury with the bulb of <s>nāginī</s>, combined with red <s>citraka</s>,
in the quantity for smearing a sheet: silver and copper become gold.
Likewise, combined with golden mica, its luster is killed.
Combined with red <s>citraka</s>, it is supreme for accomplishing bodily perfection.
Listen, O goddess, to the divine herb famed as <s>kaṭutumbī</s>.
Having gathered its seeds, one should make them into a fine powder.
Taking oil like castor oil, ground with mercury,
by that alone silver sheets become gold with just three heating-packets.
I shall state the method for <s>kṣīrakanda</s>, supreme for bringing about all attainments.
Among the four colors, the red bulb is praised.
When broken, it exudes milk, beautiful and red in color,
with seven leaves, oily like <s>snuhī</s>, and very bright like gold.
The binding of the king of mercury brings all the world under control.

children.text: toyamadhye vinikṣipya guṭikā sā ca tadbhavet ||
children.translated_text: Having placed it in water, that pill becomes such.
Pressing out the excellent juice of the <s>śāka</s> tree, O goddess,
combined with red sandalwood, it digests all metals.
One should apply it in the sun with the odor of fragrant stone.
All metals unite; they melt like water.
Sulphur, calamine, copper pyrites, mercury, and red sandalwood,
combined with the juice of <s>rudantī</s>, make silver become gold.
One should carefully filter the exudation of the <s>śāka</s> tree.
Then powder of <s>śigru</s> root should be ground with that juice.
Having smeared copper sheets and placed them in a heating-packet, one should cook them thoroughly.
After removing them, there is divine gold endowed with all marks.
One should collect the ripe fruits of the <s>śāka</s> tree.

children.text: tadrasena sūtaṃ mardyaṃ saptarātraṃ tu bhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: With their juice, mercury should be ground and infused for seven nights.
Madder and red sandalwood, combined with that juice,
should be smeared on silver sheets; when smelted, it becomes gold.
I shall state the further method of the great herb <s>devadālī</s>.

children.text: sā śvetā vyādhiśamane kṛṣṇā pītā rasāyane ||
children.translated_text: The white one is for pacifying disease; the black and yellow are for rasāyana.
<s>Devadālī</s> fruit, <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>, and mercury

children.text: mūrchayed vedhayet kṣipraṃ śulvaṃ hemaṃ karoti ca ||
children.translated_text: should be stupefied; it quickly pierces, and makes copper into gold.
Powder of <s>devadālī</s> fruit and the juice of <s>īśvarī</s>,
infused with <s>devadālī</s> juices, make tin firm in an instant.
Taking <s>devadālī</s> juice together with <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>,

children.text: vadhyate pāradaṃ caiva tāraṃ hemaṃ karoti ca ||
children.translated_text: mercury is bound, and it makes silver into gold.
Taking <s>devadālī</s> juice and fragrant stone as well,
one should liquefy all metals and bind mercury.
Now the preparation of <s>aparājitā</s>.

children.text: aparājitā ca loke'smin khyātā ca girikarṇikā
children.translated_text: <s>Aparājitā</s>, in this world, is also renowned as <s>girikarnikā</s>.
It was declared by those names by the great-souled <s>Nārada</s>.

children.text: puṣye samuddhṛtā yatnād vijayāṃ ca śubhāvahām
children.translated_text: When carefully uprooted under <s>Puṣya</s>, it is victorious and brings auspiciousness.
Having quickly uprooted it and gathered it, one should protect it with full concentration.
One should always place it in a dry corner, in a clean place.
Now the preparation of <s>brahmadaṇḍī</s>.
It is renowned as <s>brahmadaṇḍī</s>, and by name as <s>adhaḥpuṣpī</s>.

children.text: tasyā bhedadvayaṃ proktaṃ śvetā kṛṣṇā tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: Two varieties of it are taught: white and black likewise.
The root of this <s>brahmadaṇḍī</s>, wrapped with a black thread,
when tied on a person's ear, destroys tertian fever.
Now the preparation of <s>aśvagandhā</s>.
It is held to be a remedy protecting the three worlds and producing every attainment.
Seven palas of <s>aśvagandhā</s>, six palas of <s>tālī</s>,
and eight palas of jaggery having been added, the wise man should make a sweet ball.
He should eat it together with sixty-day rice, milk, and also mung-bean broth.
In three weeks his face becomes bright like a hundred-petalled lotus.
Powder of <s>aśvagandhā</s>, mixed with juice of <s>dhātrī</s>,
combined with licorice, should always be licked with honey.
By using it for six months, he is free from wrinkles and grey hair.

children.text: yojanānāṃ śataṃ gacchet śramastasya na jāyate
children.translated_text: He may go a hundred yojanas, and fatigue does not arise in him.
One pala of powdered <s>aśvagandhā</s>, and the same amount of powdered <s>balā</s>,

children.text: śatāvaryāḥ samaṃ cūrṇaṃ tadrasena tu bhāvitam
children.translated_text: with an equal powder of <s>śatāvarī</s>, should be infused with its own juice.
For just one month he should lick it together with honey.
Free from wrinkles and grey hair, he possesses the strength of nine elephants.
<s>Aśvagandhā</s>, sesame, and black gram, combined together with honey:
by using them for a month and a half, he fights with elephants.
He is a hero with the strength of nine elephants, like <s>Garuḍa</s> in speed.
Now the preparation of <s>muṣalī</s>.
This <s>muṣalī</s>, having powerful potency at its base, destroys great diseases.

children.text: guṇaṃ tasyāḥ pravakṣyāmi ye na jānanti sādhakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall declare its virtue, which practitioners do not know.
Golden-flowered, fair, <s>musalī</s>, and having betel-nut-like leaves,

children.text: nāśayanī kṣīravahā nāmabhiḥ sā śubhā matā ||
children.translated_text: destroyer, milk-bearing: by these names that auspicious one is known.
When the lunar mansion <s>Puṣya</s> is joined, one should make a fine powder.
With the application of honey, it is digested; thereafter one should subsist on milk.
By using it for one month, one is free from wrinkles and grey hair.
Or, by using it with ghee, it destroys severe skin disease.
Combined with hot water, it destroys indigestion and the like.

children.text: visūcikāṃ virekaṃ ca naśyati nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It destroys cholera and purging; there is no doubt about this.
Two parts of wheat flour, and one part of <s>musalī</s>,
having made that full of ghee, one should place it in a honey jar.
For three nights one should eat it, the destroyer of all diseases.
Now the preparation called <s>śṛṅkhalā</s>.

children.text: aśvatthaṃ badarī bhiṇḍī mākṣikaṃ kukkuṭāsthi ca
children.translated_text: <s>Aśvattha</s>, jujube, <s>bhiṇḍī</s>, pyrite, and chicken bone,

children.text: meṣaśṛṅgasya yogena vajraṃ tu mriyate kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: with the combination of ram's horn, make diamond die in an instant.
Orpiment should be infused seven times with the juices of night-roaming creatures.

children.text: vaṅgaṃ ca ghātayet tena tārapatraṃ ca lepayet ||
children.translated_text: With that one should kill tin and smear a sheet of silver.

children.text: tadvaṅgena hataṃ tāraṃ tāmre vai lepayettadā
children.translated_text: Then, with that killed tin, one should smear the silver on copper.

children.text: tattāre sūtakaṃ sarvaṃ bandhanaṃ jāyate tadā ||
children.translated_text: In that silver, all mercury then comes to be bound.
By sixty-four applications, it should produce piercing of copper.
That copper becomes silver, serving <s>dharma</s>, desire, and wealth.
Now the preparation of <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>.
<s>Bhairava</s> said:
Detached, marvelous, causing wonder among the wise in the world,
this supreme great rasāyana is renowned as <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>.
Having collected its seeds, one should then dry them in the sun.

children.text: cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā tato bījaṃ tailaṃ tasmāt samuddharet ||
children.translated_text: Having made the seed into powder, one should extract oil from it.
One should put in half as much ghee as oil, joined with a quarter as much honey.
Milk equal to the essence of buttermilk, and cow urine should be twice as much.
One should cook it over a moderate fire, and reduce it until only the oil remains.
Nutmeg, camphor, cardamom, and likewise <s>kakkolaka</s>,

children.text: etāni samabhāgāni karṣam ekaṃ tu cūrṇayet
children.translated_text: these, in equal parts, one karṣa, should be powdered.

children.text: prakṣipya tailamadhye tu ekaṃ kṛtvā sureśvari ||
children.translated_text: Having put them into the oil and made it one compound, O queen of the gods,
one should place it in an oily vessel and set it in a heap of grain.
Thirty palas, or sixty, and likewise eighty or ninety:

children.text: śataṃ vāpyadhikaṃ vāpi triṃśannyūnaṃ na kārayet
children.translated_text: one may make a hundred or even more, but should not make less than thirty.
After twenty-one days, in a windless place,
at an auspicious moment, with body purified, one should drink a pala at sunrise.
When the day has passed, he should sleep, and his food should be milk with sixty-day rice.

children.text: tṛṣitaṃ pāyayet kṣīraṃ pāyasaṃ caiva dāpayet
children.translated_text: If thirsty, he should be given milk to drink, and rice pudding should also be given.
He becomes possessed of splendor equal to the sun; he becomes always like <s>Sadāśiva</s>.

children.text: dūrasthaḥ śṛṇute vākyaṃ viṣaṃ jīryati nityaśaḥ
children.translated_text: He hears speech from far away; poison is constantly digested.

children.text: hanti cāṣṭādaśān kuṣṭhān sarvān rogāṃśca nāśayet ||
children.translated_text: It destroys the eighteen kinds of skin disease and removes all illnesses.
Hear also the result of its fourth month.
With his urine and feces one should smear copper sheets.
One should burn them by sealed heating; they become seedless gold.
Hear truly, O goddess, the result of using it for five months.

children.text: brahmatvaṃ jāyate tasya śarīraṃ nūtanaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Brahmāhood arises for him, and his body becomes new.
By six months, bodiless perfection occurs, and not otherwise.
He lives as long as the lifetime of <s>Brahmā</s>; no hesitation should be entertained here.

children.text: sevate saptamāsaṃ tu yo devi suvinītavān ||
children.translated_text: Whoever, O goddess, well disciplined, serves it for seven months,
with senses conquered and anger conquered, lives as long as <s>Maheśvara</s>.
For your pleasure, O great goddess, the path to liberation has been shown.
This supreme secret rasāyana is to be carefully concealed.
A man overcome by idleness should not perform the rite at all.
But among all herbs, it is the unsurpassed rasāyana.
By the power of this preparation, there is no place where that is not produced.
There is no rasāyana at all higher than this, nor any other.

children.text: durlabhaṃ triṣu lokeṣu satyaṃ satyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: It is hard to obtain in the three worlds; this is true, true, without doubt.
It has been declared the essence beyond the essence; out of affection for you it has been revealed.
Now the preparation of white <s>arka</s>.
Listen carefully, O <s>Pārvatī</s>, to the well-guarded supreme medicine.
Among all herbs, white <s>arka</s> is the highest medicine.

children.text: vidhānaṃ tasya vakṣyāmi kathyamānaṃ śṛṇuṣva tat
children.translated_text: I shall state its procedure; listen to it as it is being told.
Out of affection for you, and wishing for the welfare of the worlds, I speak.

children.text: tasya kṣīrarasaṃ grāhyaṃ sūtaṃ tenaiva mardayet
children.translated_text: Its milky sap should be taken, and mercury should be ground with just that.
A wise man should use it for twenty-one days.
Freed from wrinkles and grey hair, free from old age and disease,
he obtains the strength of nine elephants, becomes all-knowing, and is victorious.

children.text: pañcāṅgaṃ tasya saṃgṛhya chāyāśuṣkaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: Having gathered its five parts, one should dry them in the shade.

children.text: sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā ghṛtena madhunā saha ||
children.translated_text: Then, making them into a fine powder, together with ghee and honey,
one becomes completely free from all diseases; of this there is no doubt.
He obtains the strength of nine elephants and, in splendor, is like another sun.
By use for six months he would reach freedom from old age and death.
He should live always on milk, avoiding wind and heat.
He should avoid pungent, sour, sharp, insipid, astringent, and alkaline things.
By this very procedure the practitioner becomes a sharer in accomplishment.
Now the preparation of sulphur.
The blessed goddess said:
O god, graciously tell the procedure for sulphur.

children.text: kasmin kāle samutpannaḥ kena cotpāditaḥ purā ||
children.translated_text: At what time did it arise, and by whom was it produced in ancient times?
Those on earth who are short-lived, afflicted by old age and poverty,

children.text: teṣāṃ hitāya bhagavan saukhyatvaṃ kathaya prabho ||
children.translated_text: for their benefit, O blessed lord, tell the means of happiness, O master.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
Listen, O goddess; I shall explain how sulphur arose.
I shall fully tell you; listen, O wide-eyed one.
When the ocean of milk was being churned by the gods, O lovely-faced one,
sulphur arose there, endowed with a divine form.
By the smell of that sulphur all the gods were bewildered.

children.text: gandhaka iti samākhyātaḥ nāmnā loke babhūva ha ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by the name sulphur, it became known in the world.

children.text: tasya varṇaṃ tu jānīhi trividhaṃ cārulocane
children.translated_text: Know its color to be threefold, O beautiful-eyed one:

children.text: pītaṃ caiva tathā śvetaṃ kapotaṃ vai tṛtīyakam ||
children.translated_text: yellow, white, and pigeon-colored as the third.
In order, they are the best, middling, and inferior in power.
A purified person should employ the best, pure sulphur.
Having performed emesis and purgation, one should then undertake the rasāyana.

children.text: bhojanāni ca vakṣyāmi bhakṣyamāṇāni yāni ca ||
children.translated_text: I shall state the foods that are to be eaten.
<s>Ṣaṣṭika</s> rice, or else <s>śāli</s> rice, and especially wheat,

children.text: chāgalāni ca māṃsāni sadā pathyāni dehinām ||
children.translated_text: and goat meat are always wholesome for embodied beings.

children.text: yavānmudgāṃśca bhuñjīta kṣīraṃ madhu tathā ghṛtam
children.translated_text: One should eat barley and mung beans, and milk, honey, and ghee.
This, O goddess, is always wholesome; one should always avoid what is unwholesome.
One should avoid excessively sharp and astringent foods, oil, and sour gruel,

children.text: lavaṇāmlaṃ ca śākaṃ ca vidagdhānnaṃ ca varjayet ||
children.translated_text: as well as salt, sour food, greens, and spoiled cooked food.

children.text: amṛtaṃ ca viṣaṃ caiva kāmaṃ sūtakagandhakam ||
children.translated_text: Mercury and sulphur may indeed be either nectar or poison.
When joined with the proper procedure it is nectar; without the procedure it is poison.
The practitioner who desires accomplishment and consumes it, O goddess,
should eat it daily according to rule; it bestows the fruits of all desires.
First, sulphur should be taken, one pala in weight, resembling beryl.
Mixing it with <s>vātāri</s> oil and with the juice of <s>triphala</s>,
the wise man should consume sulphur, which destroys old age and poverty.
By use for one month, O beloved, it destroys the eighteen kinds of skin disease,
as well as wind-related abdominal lumps, wasting disease, spleen disease, and fistula.
It destroys the eighty wind disorders and diseases of the blood.
By use for six months it destroys wrinkles and grey hairs.
Youth returns again, and the hair on the head becomes like bees.
He has divine sight and great splendor, like a second <s>Śaṅkara</s>.

children.text: gandhakasya palaikaṃ tu pibet kṣīreṇa saṃyutam
children.translated_text: One should drink one pala of sulphur combined with milk.
By use for six months it destroys ringworm and itching.
By use for a year it destroys old age and death.

children.text: gavyaṃ ghṛtaṃ palaikaṃ tu tadarddhaṃ gandhakasya ca ||
children.translated_text: One pala of cow's ghee, and half that of sulphur,
by use for three months, produces a divine body.
Thus it should be done by the wise according to the number of months.
By use for a year one lives for three hundred years.

children.text: gandhakasya palārdhaṃ ca sūtakasya palaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: Half a pala of sulphur and likewise one pala of mercury,
one pala of sulphur and three palas of <s>kanyā</s>,
three palas of <s>mākṣika</s> and fourteen palas of sugar:
by use for one month, one is free from all diseases.
After six months it destroys grey hair, and a man becomes able to assume any desired form.

children.text: gandhakasya palaṃ caikaṃ rasasyāpi palaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: One pala of sulphur and likewise one pala of mercury,
three palas of <s>kanyā</s> and three palas of garlic,
and half a pala of sugar: by use for six months,
a man becomes free from all ailments and firm-bodied.
Sulphur, mica, and mercury, infused with the juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>,
one karṣa of mica should be infused seven times with milk.
Smelted in a blind crucible, it destroys old age and poverty.

children.text: gandhakaṃ tālapiṣṭaṃ ca rasaṃ bījena mardayet ||
children.translated_text: Sulphur, orpiment paste, and mercury should be ground with seed.
The discerning man should keep it placed in the earth for one month.
When it has gone into a blind crucible and has been blown upon, with a coating of silver it becomes gold.
One should eat <s>āroṭa</s> daily; it increases strength and splendor.
That, O goddess, combined with <s>triphala</s>, is supreme and produces divine sight.
And mercury joined with <s>kācamācī</s> will be killed.
Sulphur joined with <s>kācamācī</s> removes ringworm and scab.
With the odor of sulphur-stone one should separate it by means of iron.
When it has been mixed, all metals melt like water.
Sulphur, calamine, copper pyrites, mercury, and red sandalwood,
combined with the juice of <s>rudantī</s>, make silver become gold.
Sulphur joined with red ochre, and mercury in equal portion,
combined with <s>devadālī</s>, make copper become gold.

children.text: śvetābhraṃ gandhakaṃ sūtaṃ hiṅgulaṃ tālakaṃ samam
children.translated_text: White mica, sulphur, mercury, cinnabar, and orpiment in equal portions,
combined with the milk of <s>vajrī</s>, are supreme for fixing tin.
With yellow sulphur, and mercury ground with betel,
one should kill copper leaves; after they have rested, the wise man should coat them.
By heating with forest cow-dung cakes, when cool, one should infuse it three times.

children.text: nirbījaṃ tu samākhyātaṃ hemaṃ bhavati śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: It is said to be seedless; it becomes beautiful gold.

children.text: kim atra cintyaṃ yadi pītagandhakaṃ palāśaniṣṭhīvitakalkamarditam
children.translated_text: What is there to wonder at, if yellow sulphur, ground with paste spat out upon <s>palāśa</s>,

children.text: āraṇyakasyopalapācitaṃ śubhaṃ karoti tāraṃ tripuṭena kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: well cooked with forest cow-dung cakes, turns silver into gold by three puṭas?
Having made powder of glass and borax, one should coat it with the juice of <s>apāmārga</s> and plantain.

children.text: vajrāṇyekaviṃśativārāṇi tataś cūrṇena dolāsvedanena vajrāṇi dravanti ||
children.translated_text: For twenty-one times on diamonds; then, by powder and by steaming in a swing-apparatus, the diamonds melt.
And mica too melts in twenty times.

children.text: pūrvoktadolāsvedanaṃ yathā payasā ghṛtena madhunā tailena hanti śayānaṃ ca gandhakam ||
children.translated_text: The previously stated steaming in a swing-apparatus, with milk, ghee, honey, and oil, destroys dormant sulphur.

children.text: cūrṇaṃ krameṇa kadalyapāmārgatilamākṣikakṣārāṇi catvāri kācacūrṇaṃ kṛtvā mūṣāyām ardhacūrṇaṃ tu kṛtvā tasyopari kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: In order, make powder of the four alkalis of plantain, <s>apāmārga</s>, sesame, and <s>mākṣika</s>; having made glass powder, place half the powder in a crucible and put it above that.
One māṣa of powdered tuttha, and an equal copper leaf,

children.text: kharparaṃ ca tathā māṣaṃ dattvā tasyopari kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: and likewise one māṣa of kharpara: having put them there, one should place them above it.
After adding glass powder again, one should then seal the crucible.
Then, having blown it in a cow-dung fire until the copper becomes liquid,

children.text: tat tāmraṃ ca bhavetpītamaṣṭavarṇaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: that copper becomes yellow, eight-colored; there is no doubt.
Sulphur joined with <s>punarnavā</s> destroys the threefold poison.
Drunk together with cow's ghee, it surely destroys poison.
Joined with castor oil, it destroys <s>grahaṇī</s> disease.
Joined with iron dust, it destroys anemia.
Combined with pomegranate, it removes diarrhea.

children.text: guḍena saha pītaṃ tatpāmāṃ nāśayate kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: Drunk together with molasses, it destroys scab at once.
What is the use of saying much here? Together with ghee and honey,
by use for six months, it destroys old age and poverty.
Now the preparation of <s>tālaka</s>.

children.text: tālakaṃ cottamaṃ prāpya triṣu lokeṣu durlabham
children.translated_text: Having obtained excellent orpiment, rare in the three worlds,
the wise man should take the orpiment and wash it with rice-water.
Having prepared it thus with effort, he should grind it with sixty rice-grains,
and, placing it in vessels of water, should lower it so that it is well covered.

children.text: tenaiva rasapiṣṭena pūpāṃ kṛtvā paced budhaḥ
children.translated_text: With that very mercury paste the wise man should make cakes and cook them.
He should eat them with honey and ghee for seven nights; there is no doubt.
His form becomes like the rising sun, increasing attractiveness.
By three sevens alone, wrinkles and grey hairs disappear.
He becomes like heated gold, and his hairs like bees.
Having become as strong as a young elephant, he lives as long as the moon and stars.
When the month of <s>Āṣāḍha</s> has arrived, one should deposit it in a lotus-pond.

children.text: kārttike caiva samprāpte śobhane divase śubham ||
children.translated_text: And when <s>Kārttika</s> has arrived, on a fair and auspicious day,
in conjunction with an auspicious lunar mansion, one should grind it together with mercury.
And day by day one should eat it continuously for one month.
When the first week is complete, this sign appears:
he has the color of heated gold and the form of a sixteen-year-old.
Intelligent, fortunate, and prosperous, he lives for three hundred years.

children.text: dvitīye saptake caiva bhramarā iva mūrddhajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the second week, his head-hairs are like bees.
By use for one month he attains the state of a sky-goer.
Having taken neem wood, the wise man should make it hollow.

children.text: tālaṃ saṃsthāpya tanmadhye goṣṭhe ca nikhanettvidam ||
children.translated_text: He should place orpiment in its middle and bury it in a cow-stall.
After more than a month, he should take it up and grind it together with mercury.
He should eat it day by day, each month with betel leaves.
In twenty-one days it removes the eighteen kinds of skin disease.
Free from wrinkles and grey hair, devoid of old age and disease,
shining like the rising sun, he attains the state of a sky-goer.
One should place orpiment and rice in a potsherd puṭa.
Then it should be carefully wrapped with buffalo dung.
One should cook the orpiment until it becomes odorless.
Having made that paste into a ball with the juice of citron,
and having combined it with mercury, one should make it one and grind it thoroughly.
Until the paste disappears, for that long in the mortar, for four days,
afterwards it should be heated for four days inside a citron.

children.text: aṣṭāṃśena tato baddhaṃ viddhi kāntena buddhimān
children.translated_text: Then, bound with one eighth part, know it with magnetite, O wise man.

children.text: narendra surayā siktaṃ tāraṃ bhavati śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: O king, silver sprinkled with liquor becomes beautiful.
And orpiment together with mercury, combined with citron juice,
the wise man should consume in betel continuously for one month.
Having chewed the yellow preparation, he should smear sheets of silver with it.
By applying it three times and cooking it in a sealed heating, it becomes gold.
With the juice of betel alone he should grind it day after day:
orpiment joined with mercury, with citron juice alone.
Using that at the three twilights, he should make an excellent pill.

children.text: puṭapākena pītena tāraṃ hemaṃ karoti ca ||
children.translated_text: By the yellow sealed heating it makes silver into gold.
He should combine orpiment and mercury and grind them thoroughly.
Having placed it in a heap of grain, after a month it becomes able to withstand fire.

children.text: tata uddhṛte mukhe kṣipraṃ sadyaḥ khecaratāṃ nayet
children.translated_text: Then, when it has been taken out, if he quickly puts it in the mouth, it at once brings about the state of moving in the sky.
One should cook orpiment with cow dung and buffalo dung.
But when it has been ground in an iron vessel with curds and milk,

children.text: tālakaṃ surasaikena dattvā ca kharpare punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should place the orpiment with a single measure of <s>surasa</s> in a potsherd again.
Kindling the fire with goat dung, together with five measures of buffalo dung,
one should cook the orpiment until it becomes odorless.
Then, having taken it out and bound it again with the juice of citron,
one should combine it with mercury and grind it, making it one mass.
It becomes a destroyed paste, as long as it is steamed for three days.
With just an eighth part of that, one should pierce copper by the process of penetration.

children.text: narendra surayā siktaṃ śulvaṃ tāraṃ karoti ca
children.translated_text: O king, copper sprinkled with liquor makes silver.
The wise man should cook mercury fixed with orpiment in a citron.
The wise man should consume a prastha of it, well consecrated with mantras, for one month.

children.text: tāmbūlaṃ pītayā yuktaṃ sīsake śulvake'pi ca
children.translated_text: Betel joined with the yellow preparation, when applied to lead and also to copper,

children.text: kāñcanaṃ kurute divyaṃ puṭena tu na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: makes divine gold by a sealed heating; there is no doubt.
Now the procedure for raktavajrī.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā caivaṃ taruṃ divyaṃ vajrīrūpeṇa saṃsthitam
children.translated_text: Having seen such a divine tree, standing in the form of <s>vajrī</s>,
one should duly collect its excellent red sap in a bitter gourd.
There, mercury digested with magnetic ore and assimilated with a quarter of gold
the wise man should grind with that red sap for three ghaṭikās.
Having put it into a blind crucible, he should blow it with a khadira-wood fire.
Having taken the pill from inside the crucible, he should place it in his mouth.
In that very moment the accomplishment of a sky-roaming female adept arises; there is no doubt.

children.text: athavā sūtake devi tena raktena mardayet ||
children.translated_text: Or else, O goddess, he should grind mercury with that red sap
until it becomes a lump, and then he should have it blown with a khadira-wood fire.
Remaining without uncertainty, he should smear copper with it.
When that has been processed by sealed heating, it becomes gold, free from defect.
With eleven colors it removes poverty in an instant.

children.text: athaitad bhakṣayet sūkṣmaṃ cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā vicakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Now the discerning man should eat this after making it into a fine powder.
It should be given with betel, combined with the four aromatics.
In three periods of seven days it makes one free from all diseases.
By use for six months, a body like diamond is produced.
Now the procedure for uccaṭā.
I shall teach a rasāyana that is difficult even for the gods to obtain.
O lord of herbs, <s>uccaṭā</s> arises on the surface of the earth.
Endowed with four marks, its form is now described.
It has a single stalk, and in color it is like a bamboo tube.
Its flower is red, with a brilliance like a parrot’s beak.
Its bulb resembles a tortoise; such is its mark.
Having climbed upon the tree, he looks out over the ten directions.
And he sees divine forms; having seen such a mark,

children.text: rasaṃ ca madhuraṃ caiva sravate sā nirantaram
children.translated_text: a sweet juice flows from it continuously.
That juice penetrates all metals when they are smeared once.

children.text: kāñcanaṃ kurute divyaṃ kṣipraṃ caiva tu vahninā
children.translated_text: It quickly makes divine gold by means of fire.
If a man once applies the paste with the nails at the tips of his fingers, then instantly
all his skin is shed, along with all his nails and hair.

children.text: jāte tu sarvagātre tu vṛddho'pi taruṇākṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When this occurs over the whole body, even an old man has the appearance of a youth.
In the world he is like <s>Pradyumna</s>, with the valor of ten thousand elephants.
He is intelligent, knows all śāstras, and is free from wrinkles and grey hair.

children.text: mārkaṇḍaṃ iva dīrghāyuḥ satyaṃ saubhāgyavān bhavet ||
children.translated_text: He becomes long-lived like <s>Mārkaṇḍa</s>, truthful, and fortunate.

children.text: athavā patrapuṣpāṇi phalaṃ mūlaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Or else, its leaves, flowers, fruit, and root as well

children.text: sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā prativāpaṃ ca dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: should then be made into a fine powder and given as an admixture.
It should be sprinkled twenty-one times with cow urine.

children.text: kharadāhaṃ kṛte caiva hemaṃ bhavati śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: When a strong burning is performed, it becomes beautiful gold.

children.text: śulve tāre pralipte ca vedhate nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: When smeared on copper and silver, it penetrates them; there is no doubt.

children.text: kāñcanaṃ jāyate divyaṃ tribhir doṣair vivarjitam ||
children.translated_text: Divine gold arises, free from the three defects.
Now, being attentive, I shall describe a little about that herb.
On lovely <s>Kumeru</s> mountain, delightful, at a meeting-place of tīrthas,

children.text: himālaye śubhe ramye tathā jālandhare girau
children.translated_text: in the auspicious and lovely <s>Himālaya</s>, and likewise on <s>Jālandhara</s> mountain,

children.text: siddhau vindhye mahābhāge sthāne ca ramaṇīyake ||
children.translated_text: at the accomplished <s>Vindhya</s>, O greatly fortunate one, and in a charming place,
on the mountain named <s>Candrakānta</s> and at <s>Hemaprastha</s>, O fair-vowed one,
in these places the herb is famed and worshiped by the gods.

children.text: vijayā nāma vikhyātā triṣu lokeṣu pārvati
children.translated_text: It is famed by the name <s>Vijayā</s> in the three worlds, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
Worshiped by the gods, it grants long life to the chief practitioner.
Having prepared mercury digested with magnetic ore, or else digested with gold,

children.text: uccaṭāyā rasaṃ dattvā rasakarṣaṃ tu mardayet ||
children.translated_text: and adding the juice of <s>uccaṭā</s>, he should grind a karṣa of mercury.
He should drink it mixed with honey and ghee; he becomes unconscious for a moment.
Then siddhi emerges, with a radiance equal to the brilliance of the sun.
Or else, roasted mercury, with mercury as a fourth part,
Having given it the juice of <s>uccaṭā</s>, one should grind it for the space of a watch.
The mercury is killed by the heat of the sun through the power of the divine herb,
and it penetrates all metals at one part in a hundred thousand, O lovely-faced one.

children.text: athavā tāṃ kṣipedvaktre hyadṛśyo jāyate naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or else one should place that in the mouth; a man becomes invisible.
Now the preparation of <s>kuṣmāṇḍī</s>.

children.text: asti kaṅkaṇake deśe āryā bhagavatī hi sā
children.translated_text: In the region of <s>Kaṅkaṇaka</s> there is that noble blessed goddess.

children.text: tasyāḥ pūrvottare caiva dhanvantarī guhā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: To her northeast there is the cave of <s>Dhanvantarī</s>.
There the divine herb named <s>kuṣmāṇḍakī</s> is established,
for the delight of people and for the welfare of the body.
With sincere disposition one should rub a leaf of the divine herb with the hand.
From its juice the hand certainly becomes vermilion-colored.

children.text: evaṃ hi pratyayaṃ dṛṣṭvā lohaṃ tallepayedbudhaḥ
children.translated_text: Having seen this proof, the wise man should smear metal with it.

children.text: vahnimadhye dhamettaṃ tu dahet tīvrena vahninā ||
children.translated_text: He should blow it in the midst of fire and burn it with intense fire.
It becomes divine gold, adorned with divine ornaments.
The juice of that herb should be taken, and mercury should be ground with it.
By the power of the divine herb it becomes fine gold.
Having seen this proof, one should consume it for one month.
He becomes prosperous and has the body of <s>Kāmadeva</s>; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: strī vāpi puruṣo vāpi ṣaṇmāsād vyādhivarjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whether woman or man, after six months one is free from disease.
By this one produces a divine form; there is no doubt about this.
One should eat the herb; the proper food is with goat’s milk.
The juice of that herb is a fixer of mercury; with it one should again smelt tin.
That excellent tin is killed and effects penetration at one part in a thousand.
Now the preparation of <s>īśvarī</s>.

children.text: śṛṇu pārvati yatnena yathāvat kathayāmi te
children.translated_text: Listen carefully, O <s>Pārvatī</s>; I shall explain it to you as it is.
Understand properly the greatness of the <s>īśvarī</s> preparation.
I shall also state its marks, with its reed-like leaves, O beautiful one.
It has a black stalk, and its leaves resemble betel leaves.
It also has yellow flowers like gold; by these marks one should recognize it.
Because poverty is driven away by it, that very plant is regarded as <s>īśvarī</s>.
Because it subdues snakes, it is called <s>nāgadamanī</s>.

children.text: karoti nirviṣaṃ kṣipraṃ nāsye pāṇau niyojayet
children.translated_text: It quickly neutralizes poison; one should apply it in the mouth or on the hand.
When it is on the body, O goddess, it removes poison from stationary and moving creatures.
When it is present on a person’s body, it removes all quantities of poison.

children.text: ghṛtena saha saṃyuktā ceśvarī hanti tatkṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: Combined with ghee, <s>īśvarī</s> destroys it at once.
Blisters, donkey-spider bites, insects, and even foul wounds,

children.text: kuṣṭhaṃ bhagandaraṃ rogaṃ gaṇḍamālāṃ ca dāruṇam ||
children.translated_text: skin disease, fistula disease, and terrible scrofulous swellings:
combined with urine it removes the eighteen kinds of skin disease.

children.text: bhakṣayed varṣam ekaṃ tu ghṛtenāloḍya vā pibet ||
children.translated_text: One should eat it for one year, or drink it after stirring it with ghee.
For a barren woman a son is born, long-lived and pleasant to behold.

children.text: prativāpaṃ kṛtaṃ vaṅge tadrase ca niṣecayet ||
children.translated_text: When a repeated addition is made in tin, one should quench it in its juice.
The root powder of <s>īśvarī</s> makes tin a fixer in three applications.
Mercury immediately takes on the color of <s>nāginī</s> and <s>bhramarāyasa</s>.
Through grinding and steaming, mercury penetrates all things.
With a paste of one sixteenth part it enters into all metals.
Having pulled up the plant with leaves and root, one should grind it with alkali of barley.
After grinding mercury with it, one should dry it in the water of <s>arka</s>.
With the juices of the <s>munivṛkṣa</s> also, one should make that paste.
That mercury penetrates all metals at one twentieth part.
One should smear copper leaves that have been sprinkled with the juice of <s>nāginī</s>.
After melting them, by quenching, it obtains purification after ten times.
<s>Kumārī</s>, <s>brahmasomā</s>, <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, and the plant with juiced leaves:
then one should perform the operation for the complete purification of metals.
Gold penetrated by the previous paste at one sixteenth part,
together with <s>nāgaghoṣa</s>, zinc, and <s>kunaṭa</s>:
having melted it, one should quench it; after ten times it obtains purification.
With the juice of <s>punarnavā</s>, combined with the juice of <s>loṇāra</s>,

children.text: niṣeko'yaṃ tridhā pūrvaṃ punaḥ śulvaṃ tridhā tridhā
children.translated_text: this quenching is first done three times, and then copper three times, three times.
One should quench the juice of <s>nāginī</s> and milk in goat’s urine.
Prepared and applied in this way, purified seven times,

children.text: tāreṇa saha deveśi rasaṃ ca drāvayedbudhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise man should melt the mercury together with silver, O queen of gods.
Of the two, one should use one fourteenth part and half as much silver.
Divine gold is produced, with the brilliance of the young sun.
Juice of <s>nāginī</s>, juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, and <s>apāmārga</s>,

children.text: snuhīkṣīraṃ sūtakaṃ ca lavaṇāni ca pañca ca ||
children.translated_text: milk of <s>snuhī</s>, mercury, and the five salts:
ground together into a ball, one should steam it for seven nights.

children.text: evaṃ kṛte na sandeho nirmukho gaganaṃ graset ||
children.translated_text: When this is done, without doubt, mouthless, it consumes <s>gagana</s> (mica).
The operation with <s>īśvarī</s>, and the mercury and the rasāyana,
succeeds; there is no doubt about this, said <s>Parameśvara</s>.
The tasting and preparation of mercurial substances, and likewise minerals subordinate to mercury,
poisons, secondary poisons, and metals, and also the proper sequences of purification:
without the juice of divine herbs, it is not penetrated and not killed.
Mercury does not proceed anywhere, O goddess, as stated by <s>Īśvara</s>.
At the time of taking it, the food should be milk and <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice.
I shall explain the binding of mercury, by which the practitioner succeeds.
One pala of mercury should be taken, and likewise one pala of mica.
Having extracted the juice of <s>nāginī</s>, and goat’s urine as well,
the wise man should boil it with fire; then he should grind it into copper.
The ground ball should be steamed for a day and night, O <s>Maheśvarī</s>.

children.text: guṭikā jāyate sā tu sarvalohāni vidhyati
children.translated_text: That pill is produced, and it penetrates all metals.

children.text: guṭikāṃ tāṃ mukhe kṣiptvā hyadṛśyo jāyate naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having placed that pill in his mouth, a man becomes invisible.
And by this very procedure one should grind mercury with mica.

children.text: punarmardyaṃ punaḥ khedyaṃ saptavāraṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: It should be ground again and heated again, repeatedly, seven times.
Having thus made it digested, according to the procedure of seven nights,
it becomes capable of sixty-fourfold penetration after two weeks, O <s>Sundarī</s>.
In three weeks it has hundredfold penetration, and in the fourth, indeed, ten-thousandfold.
